concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Commercial crops were prioritised over food crops during colonial rule. Which of the following is an example of a commercial crop promoted by the British?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indigo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indigo was one of the most significant commercial crops promoted by the British during colonial rule.
 
• The British encouraged indigo cultivation extensively as it was highly profitable and in demand for dyeing textiles in Europe.
 
• Farmers were often forced into growing indigo under exploitative conditions through the "Tinkathia System," where they had to dedicate a portion of their land to indigo crops.
 
• Indigo cultivation led to the exploitation of Indian farmers, causing widespread resentment and eventually leading to the Indigo Revolt (1859-1860).
 
• The prioritization of indigo and other commercial crops severely impacted food crop production, leading to famines and food shortages during colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commercial Crops:** These are crops grown primarily for sale and profit rather than for subsistence. Examples include indigo, cotton, jute, and tea.
 
• **Indigo Revolt:** A major uprising by farmers in Bengal in 1859-1860 against forced cultivation of indigo and exploitative practices by British planters.
 
• **Tinkathia System:** A system imposed by British planters where farmers had to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land compulsorily, often leading to financial distress.
 
• **Impact on Food Crops:** The emphasis on commercial crop cultivation displaced food crops, contributing to famines such as the Great Bengal Famine of 1943.
 
• **Colonial Agricultural Policies:** The British prioritized cash crops for export, neglecting the needs of local populations, which caused significant socio-economic hardships in rural India.
